requirement_summary: A penetration testing methodology is defined, documented and implemented, covering the CDE perimeter and critical systems, internal and external testing, application- and network-layer testing, segmentation validation, review of threats/vulnerabilities from the last 12 months, risk-based handling of findings, and retention of results for at least 12 months.
applicability_reasoning: Applies only if Unbound stores, processes or transmits cardholder data or can affect CDE security; card payments deferred (ODP-10); processor-hosted pages only if introduced.

requirement_summary: Internal and external penetration testing at least once every 12 months and after any significant infrastructure or application upgrade or change, performed by a qualified internal resource or qualified external third party; organizational independence of the tester must exist; the tester need not be a QSA or ASV.
applicability_reasoning: Same PCI scope dependency as REQ-PENTEST-001.

requirement_summary: Exploitable vulnerabilities and security weaknesses found during penetration testing are corrected per the entity's risk ranking (Req 6.3.1) and penetration testing is repeated to verify the corrections.
applicability_reasoning: PCI scope dependency.

requirement_summary: If segmentation is used to reduce PCI scope, segmentation controls are tested at least every 12 months (every 6 months for service providers) and after changes, by a qualified and organizationally independent tester.
applicability_reasoning: Only if segmentation is used to isolate a CDE.

requirement_summary: Multi-tenant service providers support their customers' external penetration testing (additional requirement for multi-tenant service providers).
applicability_reasoning: Wording recalled, not read from the licensed text; relevant only if Unbound is a PCI multi-tenant service provider.

framework_ref: PCI SSC Pen Testing Guidance v1.1 s.3
requirement_summary: Qualified internal resources or a qualified third party may perform the test if organizationally independent (separate from management of the target systems). Listed certifications (OSCP, CEH, GPEN, GWAPT, GXPN, CREST, CHECK) indicate competence but are not required and are not endorsed; experience must also be assessed.
applicability_reasoning: Guidance under PCI DSS; also a widely reused benchmark for tester qualification in non-PCI contexts.

requirement_summary: Penetration testing of information systems from both inside and outside the system boundaries by a qualified internal or external party at least annually, under written vulnerability-management policies informed by the risk assessment.
applicability_reasoning: Applies only to DFS-licensed/registered covered entities; Unbound licensing not determined. Small entities under 500.19(a) are exempt from 500.5.

requirement_summary: Automated vulnerability scans plus manual review of systems not covered by scans at a risk-based frequency and promptly after material changes; a monitoring process for new vulnerabilities; timely, risk-prioritised remediation.
applicability_reasoning: As REQ-PENTEST-007.

requirement_summary: Limited exemption: covered entities with fewer than 20 employees and contractors, or under US$7.5m gross annual revenue in each of the last three years, or under US$15m year-end total assets are exempt from 500.5 (and other listed sections).
applicability_reasoning: Relevant only if Part 500 applies; a small Unbound operator would likely qualify on headcount (assumption).

requirement_summary: Regularly test or otherwise monitor the effectiveness of the safeguards' key controls, systems and procedures, including those to detect actual and attempted attacks on or intrusions into information systems.
applicability_reasoning: Applies to FTC-jurisdiction financial institutions under GLBA; whether Unbound or its operator is one (or a service provider bound by contract) is a legal question.

requirement_summary: Monitoring and testing shall include continuous monitoring or periodic penetration testing and vulnerability assessments; absent effective continuous monitoring, annual penetration testing (based on identified risks) and vulnerability assessments at least every six months and after material changes.
applicability_reasoning: As REQ-PENTEST-010; continuous monitoring is an explicit alternative to annual pen testing.

requirement_summary: Financial institutions maintaining customer information concerning fewer than 5,000 consumers are exempt from 314.4(d)(2) (and (b)(1), (h), (i)).
applicability_reasoning: Consumer count of Unbound at launch unknown; DAF donors may or may not be 'customers' of the operator.

requirement_summary: Conduct penetration testing at an organization-defined frequency on organization-defined systems/components; goes beyond automated scanning; performed by agents with demonstrable skills; rules of engagement agreed in advance. Selected only in the High baseline (800-53B).
applicability_reasoning: No federal system or contract requiring 800-53 identified; useful reference catalog.

requirement_summary: Employ an independent penetration testing agent or team, free from actual or perceived conflicts of interest with development, operation or management of the target systems; risk assessment guides the level of independence (High baseline).
applicability_reasoning: Reference definition of tester independence.

requirement_summary: Establish a public reporting channel for receiving reports of vulnerabilities in organizational systems and components (in Low, Moderate and High baselines).
applicability_reasoning: Basis for a VDP; low cost.

requirement_summary: Developers perform security testing/evaluation at organization-defined depth and coverage, produce evidence, implement verifiable flaw remediation; discussion lists manual code review, security architecture review, penetration testing, static/dynamic/binary analysis and fuzzing as approaches.
applicability_reasoning: Model for internal (non-independent) developer testing.

requirement_summary: Examiner baseline: independent testing (including penetration testing and vulnerability scanning) is conducted according to the risk assessment for external-facing systems and the internal network; examiners verify management tracks and remediates findings.
applicability_reasoning: Binds banks, not Unbound; flows down via bank third-party risk management if a bank partner is involved. CAT itself sunset 2025-08-31.

requirement_summary: Current Security Rule contains no explicit penetration-testing requirement; the January 2025 NPRM proposes penetration testing at least every 12 months and vulnerability scanning every 6 months; final action projected July 2027.
applicability_reasoning: Unbound is not expected to be a covered entity or business associate (no PHI) - assumption.

requirement_summary: SOC 2 criteria do not require penetration testing; a CC4.1 point of focus lists penetration testing among example types of ongoing/separate evaluations. Points of focus are illustrative; auditors commonly expect or advise a pen test.
applicability_reasoning: SOC 2 is a design target (decision 0D02); no examination is currently planned or authorized (external engagements deferred under DF-ASR-2026-0D0F; ODP-09 plans without assuming auditor reliance); pen test is an auditor/customer expectation rather than a criterion.

requirement_summary: No explicit penetration-testing mandate; technical vulnerability management and security testing in development/acceptance controls are the usual hooks, and certification auditors may expect testing evidence where risk treatment calls for it.
applicability_reasoning: ISO 27001 not currently targeted.

requirement_summary: Federal agencies must publish a VDP authorising good-faith research, committing not to pursue legal action, describing scope, submission and expected timelines.
applicability_reasoning: Binding only on federal executive agencies; used as a design template.

requirement_summary: security.txt at /.well-known/security.txt with required Contact and Expires fields; signing recommended.
applicability_reasoning: Informational RFC; near-zero cost.
